top_signals.title: When the Grid Fails, Solar Does Not Wait for the State
top_signals.summary: Most power systems are built from the center outward. A government plans power stations. A utility signs fuel contracts, builds transmission lines and connects households. Large investors finance assets expected to operate for decades. The model assumes a state capable of making decisions, enforcing contracts and protecting infrastructure. In fragile and conflict-affected countries, those assumptions can disappear before electricity demand does. Syria offers a striking alternative. Solar panels now cover rooftops around the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.
